analysis:
Only base-side text of MediaIngest.swift was supplied (lines 1-936). No patch or head text was provided, so the actual PR change is unseen and no security conclusion about it is possible. This is a coverage limit, not evidence that the change is safe.

Base behavior relevant to T-050, A-001 and TB-003/TB-007:
- purgeLegacyVideoTempFiles (lines 37-62) removes only regular, non-symlink files named vlm-<UUID>.mp4. It runs after the single-instance lock.
- decodeVideo (779-822) accepts only data:video/mp4 or quicktime base64. It builds a MemoryBackedVideoAsset, so no plaintext file is written.
- The metadata probe and enforceVideoLimits (831-881) fail closed on duration, track dimensions and frame pixels.
- dataFromDataURI (886-934) preflights size before allocating. Caps default to 25 MiB per part, 100 MP per image and 384 MP per request, with 16 images and 8 videos per request. Env overrides are saturating.
- Image headers are charged to the aggregate cap before decode (lines 397-435).
- Non-data: URIs are rejected with invalidURL, which blocks SSRF and local-file reads. MediaError descriptions may echo up to 200 characters of the URI; the comments say they must not cross outbound logging boundaries.
- inputAudio is rejected generically. buildUserInput calls rejectUnsupportedAudio(request) without modelType (line 278), and projections return .max for audio.

Next pass should diff head against base for:
- Any reintroduction of temp files or loosened caps.
- Changes to the audio and modelType gating.
- Any logging or egress of MediaError.description.
- Changes to the percent-decode path and overflow handling.
